IN THE 
 Supreme Court of the United States 

No. 19-508 

————— 

AMG CAPITAL MANAGEMENT, LLC, ET AL.,  
PETITIONERS 

v. 

FEDERAL TRADE COMMISSION 

————— 

To the Honorable Elena Kagan, Circuit Justice for the United States Court 
of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit: 

APPLICATION FOR LEAVE TO EXCEED WORD LIMITS 

The Federal Trade Commission respectfully requests leave to file its 
brief on the merits in excess of the word limit set forth in Supreme Court 
Rule 33.1(g)(vi), not to exceed 15,500 words, with a corresponding increase 
in the reply brief, not to exceed 7,150 words.  

1.  On July 9, 2020, the Court granted the petition for certiorari in this 

case along with the Commission’s petition in No. 19-825, Federal Trade 
Commission v. Credit Bureau Center, LLC, presenting substantially the 
same question. The Court consolidated the two cases and allotted a total of 
one hour for oral argument. 

2.  The following month, the Court granted the parties’ joint motion to 

realign the parties and extend the briefing schedule. In accordance with 
that schedule, the petitioners in AMG and the respondents in Credit 
Bureau Center filed their opening briefs on September 25, 2020. Together, 
the opening briefs totaled 25,216 words on the common issue. Amici filed 
eight briefs supporting the arguments made in the opening briefs.  

3.  On November 2, 2020, the Court deconsolidated the cases and 

vacated the order granting certiorari in Credit Bureau Center.  

4.  To provide the Court with a full presentation of its arguments, the 
Commission respectfully requests to file in AMG a brief on the merits in 
excess of the Court’s ordinary word count, not to exceed 15,500 words. 
Counsel for AMG does not object to the Commission’s request for an 
increased word count.

5.  Counsel for AMG has authorized the Commission to respectfully 
request that, insofar as the Commission is granted additional words for its 
responsive brief, AMG be afforded a corresponding increase in the number 
of words for its reply brief, not to exceed 7,150 words.  The Commission 
does not object to that request. 

Accordingly, the Commission respectfully requests to adjust the word 

limits as described above.  

Respectfully submitted, 

 ALDEN F. ABBOTT 
  General Counsel 
  Counsel of Record 
JOEL MARCUS 
  Deputy General Counsel for Litigation 
MICHAEL BERGMAN 
THEODORE (JACK) METZLER 
MATTHEW M. HOFFMAN 
  Attorneys 
FEDERAL TRADE COMMISSION 
600 Pennsylvania Ave. NW 
Washington, D.C. 20580 
(202) 326-2505 
aabbott@ftc.gov 

November 12, 2020 

2
